papers.title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
papers.summary: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.
papers.tldr: 量子機械学習（QML）を用いた生成的手法が、限られた乳房超音波画像データセットを拡張し、がん検出のための分類器のトレーニングにおいて、合成画像を生成することで有効であることを示しました。合成画像のみでトレーニングした分類器は、実データのベースラインに対してAUC-ROCが0.802に達しました。

papers.title: Structural Chain-of-Thought: Reasoning with Executable Computational Graphs
papers.summary: Chain-of-thought prompting enables reasoning in large language models but produces explanations that are difficult to verify, expensive to generate, and not always faithful. We introduce a Structural Chain-of-Thought framework where models generate executable computational graphs instead of free-form reasoning. The final answer is obtained by deterministically executing the graph. The model is trained using graph-based reinforcement learning that rewards structural validity, answer correctness, and node overlap with reference graphs. Experiments across five benchmarks and four model families show that our method consistently improves accuracy over supervised graph training and can reduce generation length by up to 5-6x compared with standard GRPO and chain-of-thought supervised training. Our faithfulness experiments reveal that models trained with our approach tend to rely on deriving their answers from the generated graphs rather than producing post-hoc rationalizations as usually in chain-of-thought reasoning.
papers.tldr: 構造的チェーン・オブ・ソートフレームワークでは、モデルが自由形式の推論の代わりに実行可能な計算グラフを生成し、グラフを決定論的に実行することで最終的な回答を得る。実験により、この方法は精度を向上させ、生成長を最大5〜6倍短縮できることが示された。

papers.title: RELAGRAM: Recursive Latent Graph Model for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
papers.summary: Latent recursion repeatedly processes internal representations through the same neural network. Recent work has shown this approach to be effective on structured reasoning tasks such as Sudoku and maze solving. However, whether latent recursion can support neural routing remains unclear. We introduce RELAGRAM (Recursive Latent Graph Model), a novel approach that brings latent recursion to graph combinatorial optimization. RELAGRAM encodes a capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) instance as edge tokens; a compact transformer recurrently updates the latent representations of these tokens. An output head maps the answer state to an edge heatmap, from which an autoregressive decoder constructs a feasible solution. On CVRP-100 instances, the 0.53M-parameter RELAGRAM achieves gaps to a PyVRP reference of 13.4%, 9.8%, and 8.3% under greedy decoding, eightfold symmetry augmentation, and 256-candidate search, respectively. Trained only on CVRP-100, RELAGRAM generalizes zero-shot to CVRP-500 and CVRP-1000, achieving gaps of 15.6% and 21.7% under 256-candidate search. Together, these results demonstrate that latent recursion is a promising approach to neural routing.
papers.tldr: RELAGRAM（Recursive Latent Graph Model）は、潜在再帰を用いてキャパシタ付き車両ルーティング問題（CVRP）を解決する新しい手法であり、グラフ組合せ最適化において有望な結果を示しています。特に、CVRP-100インスタンスに対して、異なるデコーディング手法を用いることで、PyVRP参照に対して最大21.7%のギャップを達成しました。

papers.title: RegExtract: A Benchmark for PFAS Regulatory Information Extraction with LLMs
papers.summary: Extracting structured information from regulatory documents is a critical but challenging task. Relevant facts are scattered across long, legally dense texts, and traceability of extracted facts to their source is essential for verification. With increasing awareness of the environmental and health impacts of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), regulatory documents have expanded significantly, varying in scope and product relevance, making interpretation challenging for manufacturers and policymakers. We introduce RegExtract, a benchmark for structured information extraction from PFAS regulatory documents, comprising 488 human-annotated field instances across 20 US state documents and 46 regulations. Each field instance includes a value and a provenance entry, yielding 976 entries in total. We define a typed, multi-field schema targeting key elements such as material definitions, permitted uses, and product exemptions, and propose provenance-aware evaluation metrics tailored to regulatory text. Through experiments with open- and closed-source LLMs across prompting strategies, document condensing methods, and schema partitioning approaches, we find that document identification fields remain challenging, and that field-specific few-shot examples improve extraction. This work lays the groundwork for AI tools for hazardous substance identification, question answering, and compliance monitoring. The code and data are available at https://github.com/IBM/PFAS-regulations.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: RegExtractは、PFASに関する規制文書からの構造化情報抽出のためのベンチマークで、488の人間注釈付きフィールドインスタンスを含み、AIツールによる有害物質の特定やコンプライアンス監視の基盤を提供します。

papers.title: Random Feature Pruning for Multi-Class Classification
papers.summary: Weighted sums of random kitchen sinks (W-RKS) is a commonly used feature extraction technique for supervised learning tasks. A major drawback of this method is the redundancy and ineffectiveness of many extracted random features. This paper investigates efficient methods for reducing such redundancy in multi-class classification problems. We specifically formulate feature selection as a variant of the sequentially nested model selection problem and introduce the Successive Empirical Excess Risk Difference Maximization (SEED-MAX) algorithm. It recursively computes empirical risks to identify the most parsimonious yet informative set of features. We derive an analytical lower bound for the probability of correct feature selection by the SEED-MAX algorithm. This lower bound on the probability of correct feature selection can be made arbitrarily close to one by increasing the training dataset size. To further enhance the rate of pruning, we evaluate the features retained by SEED-MAX using the Fisher test (F-Test). Empirical evaluations on UCR time-series classification datasets show that the sequential application of SEED-MAX with the Fisher test achieves approximately 92 percent rate of pruning with negligible degradation in classification accuracy. Implementations of the SEED-MAX and SEED-MAX-F-Test methods are available at https://github.com/OmidiAmin/seed-max-ftest.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、W-RKSによる特徴抽出の冗長性を削減するために、SEED-MAXアルゴリズムを提案し、Fisherテストを用いて特徴選択を行うことで、分類精度をほぼ維持しつつ約92%の特徴削減を達成した。

papers.title: TIDE: Trajectory-Informed Skill Distillation for Efficient Text-to-Video Prompt Optimization
papers.summary: Text-to-video (T2V) models are highly sensitive to prompt specificity, while iterative prompt optimization typically improves generation quality only through repeated video generation and vision-language model evaluation at inference time. We propose TIDE, a framework that distills this costly search process into an interpretable and reusable prompt-rewriting Skill. TIDE formulates prompt rewriting as a set of source-conditioned rule modules, each targeting a distinct semantic dimension. Once distilled, the frozen Skill activates the relevant rules and generates both positive and negative prompts in a single LLM call, followed by only one T2V generation, without test-time visual search or backbone fine-tuning. Evolved using only 100 prompts over 14 hours, TIDE achieves prompt-optimization performance comparable to computationally expensive search-based methods. Moreover, when transferred to previously unseen video-generation models, TIDE outperforms existing approaches specifically designed or trained for those models. Code is available at https://github.com/xiningin/TIDE_T2V.
papers.tldr: TIDEは、テキストから動画へのプロンプト最適化を効率化するフレームワークで、コストのかかる探索プロセスを解釈可能で再利用可能なプロンプト書き換えスキルに蒸留します。この手法は、視覚検索やバックボーンのファインチューニングなしで、わずか1回の生成で高品質なプロンプトを生成できることを実現しています。

papers.title: Anchors Enhance Controllability and Reasoning of Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer new opportunities for controllable text generation. However, their controllability, defined as the ability to satisfy task constraints while preserving their original capabilities, remains underexplored. DLMs' bidirectional attention allows control tokens to guide generation from arbitrary positions in the output sequence, but effective guidance depends on the compatibility between their content and placement. To this end, we propose AnchorDLM, a framework in which an anchor generator produces an anchor consisting of a short output fragment and its position for each query. The anchor is placed as control tokens at the specified position to initialize the output sequence of a frozen DLM and guide subsequent denoising. We train the anchor generator with reinforcement learning (RL) to jointly optimize anchor content and placement, using rewards computed from the DLM's generated outputs based on answer correctness and constraint satisfaction. Moreover, through the lens of discrete flow matching (DFM), we interpret anchor placement as helping to reshape the initial velocity field that guides generation. Experiments on code generation and mathematical reasoning across five DLM backbones show that AnchorDLM improves controllability and further yields gains in reasoning performance across diverse benchmarks.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: AnchorDLMは、拡散言語モデルの制御性と推論能力を向上させるフレームワークで、アンカー生成器を用いて出力シーケンスの特定位置に制御トークンを配置し、強化学習で最適化を行うことで、コード生成や数学的推論の性能を改善します。

papers.title: Swarm Telepathy: Prefill-Free KV-Cache Transfer Across Families
papers.summary: LLM multi-agent systems split work across agents that communicate through text. An agent summarizes its findings, another agent receives the text. This constrains communication to discrete tokens and costs redundant compute, limiting bandwidth and capabilities of multi-agent systems. Recent works demonstrate KV-cache transfer between LLMs but they either require the LLMs to be within the same family or cannot function across context, thus requiring the receiver to prefill text. We present SwaT (Swarm Telepathy), the first cross-family KV-cache transfer method that allows prefill-free communication in multi-family multi-agent systems. In an agent-to-agent communication setting, combining SwaT with recent advances in KV-cache compaction beats text-to-text communication in both accuracy and speed, with a mean of $40\%$ higher accuracy and a mean of $4\times$ faster wall-clock time. Experiments show SwaT achieves high performance on 17 benchmarks across 12 LLMs and 6 families. Additionally, given a sender Vision-Language Model (VLM), SwaT is able to transfer the vision capabilities to a text-only receiver LLM exceeding text-to-text communication despite SwaT being trained on text-only data. SwaT keeps both sender and receiver models frozen without fine-tuning and only requires $<50M$ tokens and $<1$ GPU-day to train.
papers.tldr: SwaT（Swarm Telepathy）は、異なるファミリー間でのKVキャッシュ転送を可能にする初の手法で、事前入力なしでのエージェント間通信を実現し、テキスト通信に比べて平均40%の精度向上と4倍の速度向上を達成します。SwaTは、視覚と言語を統合したモデルからテキスト専用モデルへの能力移転も可能で、トレーニングには50Mトークン未満と1日未満のGPU時間しか必要としません。

papers.title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents
papers.summary: AI coding agents operate in iterative loops: they modify code, run tools, inspect the results, and decide what to do next. We call the design of this process loop engineering, which includes context management, model selection, compaction, and termination. Existing efficiency work mainly compresses tool observations or routes selected turns to cheaper models, but the practical opportunity for these optimizations remains unclear. We analyze 600 publicly released coding-agent trajectories spanning two agent scaffolds and two language models. Median observations contain only 118-286 tokens, while the large build logs commonly used to motivate compression occur near the ninety-ninth percentile. Moreover, 98.6% of input tokens are served from a prefix cache, so flat input pricing overestimates loop cost by roughly 7x on average under near-ideal caching. We derive and empirically validate a closed-form break-even condition for model delegation. Delegation increases cost in half of the evaluated settings, near the predicted boundary. More broadly, turn count explains 84% of the variance in log trajectory cost, compared with 4% for mean observation size; the most expensive trajectories have the most turns despite having the smallest observations. These associations suggest that observation-focused methods target a secondary cost factor, and identify unnecessary turns as the larger and largely unexamined opportunity, though we do not establish that turns can be removed while holding task success fixed. We release TurnCost, a tool for re-scoring trajectory corpora under alternative caching, pricing, compression, and routing policies.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: TurnCostは、AIコーディングエージェントのループエンジニアリングを分析し、観察サイズよりもターン数がコストに与える影響が大きいことを示しており、ターン数の最適化が重要な機会であると提案しています。

papers.title: VLCQ: Post-training quantization for deep neural networks using variable length coding
papers.summary: Quantization plays a crucial role in efficiently deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Post-training quantization does not require access to the original dataset or retraining the full model. Current methods that achieve high performance close to baseline results typically require INT8 fixed-point integers. However, achieving higher model compression with lower bit-widths often leads to significant performance degradation. In this paper, we propose VLCQ, a post-training quantization method that relaxes the fixed-point encoding constraint, enabling more flexible exploration of quantization techniques through variable-length encoding. This approach achieves competitive or improved performance while reducing bit-widths, without requiring access to training data or model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on image classification, segmentation, and object detection demonstrate that VLCQ improves model compression and accuracy compared with state-of-the-art post-training quantization approaches. For per-channel quantization, VLCQ surpasses FP32 accuracy and Piece-Wise Linear Quantization (PWLQ) on most evaluated models, achieving up to 6x compression compared with FP32 and up to 1.7x compared with PWLQ. When prioritizing compression with limited accuracy loss, VLCQ achieves up to 12.25x compression compared with FP32 with less than 4% performance degradation. For per-tensor quantization, VLCQ is competitive with Data-Free Quantization (DFQ), while providing greater flexibility to achieve lower bit rates across different tasks and models.
papers.tldr: VLCQは、固定小数点エンコーディングの制約を緩和し、可変長エンコーディングを通じてポストトレーニング量子化を実現する手法で、従来の手法よりも高いモデル圧縮と精度を達成します。実験結果により、VLCQはFP32やPWLQと比較して最大6倍の圧縮を実現し、精度の低下を抑えつつ効率的なデプロイが可能です。

papers.title: Have You Been Convinced? A Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning Approach to Detecting Persuasiveness in ChangeMyView Discussions
papers.summary: Argument structures represent how individual arguments interact within a discourse. However, leveraging these structures to infer meaningful knowledge remains challenging, as it requires a formal representation of how argumentative influence propagates across the structure. We propose Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning System (NARS) for performing persuasiveness detection directly from online discussions. The neural component employs retrieval-augmented iterative LLM reasoning to extract bipolar argument structures, while the symbolic component applies gradual argumentation semantics to propagate argumentative influence over the structure. Using the Webis-CMV-20 corpus, we construct CMV2BAS, a dataset of long, multi-threaded ChangeMyView discussions annotated with LLM-derived bipolar argument structures and labeled with delta events (view change vs.\ no change). We investigate whether gradual argumentation semantics can effectively detect persuasiveness, whether augmenting them with argument quality and graph-based centrality improves performance, and whether symbolic reasoning remains necessary in the presence of modern LLMs. NARS achieves F1=0.57 and AUC=0.56 under its best configuration, outperforming zero-shot Qwen3.6:27B and GPT-oss:20B. We identify support-dominant discussions and long argumentative chains as key failure modes limiting attack influence propagation. Our work demonstrates the feasibility of operationalizing formal gradual argumentation semantics over noisy real-world discourse for scalable macro-level persuasion analysis, while highlighting key challenges and directions for future research in neuro-symbolic argumentation reasoning. We release both CMV2BAS dataset and the NARS framework for public use.
papers.tldr: Neuro-symbolic Argumentation Reasoning System (NARS)を用いて、オンラインディスカッションにおける説得力の検出を行う新しいアプローチを提案し、CMV2BASデータセットを構築しました。このシステムは、引き合いに出された議論の構造を解析し、説得力を評価するための有効性を示しています。

papers.title: Self-Evolving Visual Agent via Margin Reward
papers.summary: Visual agents that interleave reasoning with tool invocation have posed a promising direction for multimodal tasks. However, learning effective tool invocation usually relies on curated question-answer pairs or expert demonstrations at scale, which are expensive to acquire. In this study, we propose Marvo, a simple-yet-effective self-evolution approach that enables learning tool invocation from unlabeled images. Marvo consists of two agents: (1) a challenger that generates question-answer pairs from unlabeled images, and (2) a solver that learns tool invocation by solving questions through reinforcement learning. To encourage effective tool invocation, a good training question should be difficult enough to warrant tool use, yet remain within the solver's capabilities. To this end, we introduce a margin reward to the challenger, defined as solver's performance difference with and without access to tools. With the margin reward, we create an adaptive curriculum that encourages the solver to learn effective tool invocation. Across benchmarks covering agentic reasoning, visual search, mathematical, and general real-world reasoning, Marvo improves average accuracy by up to 7.1\% --- demonstrating margin reward as a preferred way to scale question complexity without human supervision.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: Marvoは、ラベルのない画像からツールの呼び出しを学習する自己進化型ビジュアルエージェントで、挑戦者と解決者の2つのエージェントを用いて、マージン報酬を導入することで効果的なツールの使用を促進し、平均精度を最大7.1%向上させることを示した。

papers.title: GAMW: Generation-Aware Mel-Domain Watermarking for TTS Traceability
papers.summary: As text-to-speech (TTS) systems continue to advance, provenance tracking and security verification of synthesized speech have become increasingly important. Audio watermarking provides active provenance by embedding imperceptible, machine-recoverable information into speech. However, existing post-hoc methods typically modify the waveform after synthesis, leaving the watermark vulnerable to compound perturbations. To address this limitation, we propose GAMW, a watermark injection framework integrated into the TTS generation process. Before waveform synthesis, GAMW embeds a content-adaptive multi-bit watermark residual into the generated representation, and its decoding objective combines focal modulation with dynamic per-bit weighting. We train and evaluate GAMW separately on two TTS backbones. With a 16-bit payload, GAMW improves decoding accuracy over the strongest baseline by 9.2 and 23.5 percentage points under individual and compound perturbations, respectively, while maintaining competitive speech quality. Reliable clean-speech decoding is also retained at higher payloads. Code is available at https://github.com/ZConJugaTe/GAMW.
papers.tldr: GAMWは、テキスト音声合成（TTS）プロセスに統合されたウォーターマーク注入フレームワークで、合成音声の出所追跡とセキュリティ検証を強化します。16ビットのペイロードで、従来の手法に比べてデコーディング精度を大幅に向上させつつ、音声品質も維持しています。

papers.title: Knowledge transfer between simple discrete worlds
papers.summary: Adapting to a new world and reasoning correctly about which outcomes are possible under rules one has not met before is a basic capacity underlying general intelligence. We study it in small discrete worlds: sets of grid configurations consistent with a shared set of rules, concretely Sudoku-like puzzles built from a common base and a handful of extra rules. We train a single depth-recurrent model on many combinations of rules and test it at four levels of novelty: a new puzzle, a new combination of known rules, a pairing of rules never seen together, and a rule instance not seen at all during training. The model receives the active rules either as a symbolic description or as two solved examples, and a model that gets no rule information is used as a baseline. At recombining rules it was trained on, the description matches or exceeds examples ($99\%$ against $95\%$ on new combinations). On rule instances whose components never co-occurred in training, the description falls below the no-information baseline while examples stay above it. The framework allows us to test many such generalization regimes in more systematic way than benchmarks such as ARC-AGI and provides new ground for evaluating depth-recurrent reasoning models, which are typically tested on saturated Sudoku benchmarks.
papers.tldr: 新しい世界への適応能力と未知のルールに基づく推論能力を、小さな離散的な世界（具体的には数独のようなパズル）を用いて研究し、異なるルールの組み合わせに対するモデルの一般化能力を評価した。結果、トレーニングで見たルールの再結合においては高い性能を示したが、トレーニングで未経験のルールの組み合わせでは性能が低下した。

papers.title: Region Aware Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks for Image Segmentation
papers.summary: Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) modules improve convolutional networks by modeling channel-wise dependencies, but global average pooling collapses spatial structure into a single per-channel descriptor, limiting their effectiveness for dense prediction tasks such as image segmentation. We generalize SE by replacing global pooling with spatially guided pooling, enabling region-aware channel recalibration through four modules with complementary cost profiles. BASE formalizes Tiled Squeeze-and-Excite using a regular grid; SPASE pools over SLIC superpixels for image-adaptive regions; MAPSE obtains regions from semantic maps produced by a frozen, general-purpose network; and PLEASE learns soft region assignments end-to-end through a lightweight assignment network. Each channel receives one gate per region, so attention at each pixel reflects its region membership, bridging channel and spatial attention. PLEASE also produces its soft assignments as a byproduct of the forward pass, providing structured spatial interpretability without post-hoc analysis. The modules offer complementary computational tradeoffs: some add essentially no parameters, while others add no measurable latency. Across binary segmentation on CUB, DUTS, and ECSSD, semantic segmentation on PASCAL VOC 2012 and ADE20K, and classification on mini-ImageNet, our modules outperform SE and related spatial-channel attention variants on most benchmarks, achieving the majority of best results.
papers.tldr: 地域を考慮したSqueeze-and-Excitationネットワークを用いた画像セグメンテーションにおいて、グローバルプーリングを空間的にガイドされたプーリングに置き換えることで、チャネル再キャリブレーションを実現し、従来のSEモジュールを超える性能を発揮することが示された。各モジュールは異なる計算トレードオフを提供し、さまざまなベンチマークで優れた結果を達成している。

papers.title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials
papers.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) accelerate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by learning the energies and forces that govern atomic motion. Recent work has shown that relaxing physical inductive biases can improve computational efficiency and predictive accuracy, raising the question of whether energy-and-force matching alone is sufficient to ensure accurate sampling. We show that, for unconstrained hypothesis classes, the relationship between prediction error and sampling accuracy is exponentially ill-conditioned in dimension. In particular, prediction errors that decay exponentially with dimension can coexist with nearly maximal total variation distance between the learned and target distributions. We identify two failure mechanisms. The first is kinetic trapping, where relaxation to an accurate learned equilibrium requires exponentially long times, even when simulations are initialized from training configurations at which energies and forces are matched exactly. The second is equilibrium mismatch, where the learned stationary distribution itself remains far from the target. Under explicit assumptions, we show that equilibrium mismatch can persist even in local, symmetry-preserving models, where small per-atom errors coexist with a distributional discrepancy that approaches its maximum as system size increases. Finally, we establish global energy-control conditions that guarantee equilibrium accuracy and identify additional conditions required for rapid relaxation.
papers.tldr: 機械学習による原子間ポテンシャル（MLIPs）は分子動力学シミュレーションを加速するが、エネルギーと力の一致だけでは正確なサンプリングを保証できないことが示されている。特に、予測誤差とサンプリング精度の関係が次元に対して指数的に悪条件であることが明らかになり、平衡不一致や運動的トラッピングといった失敗メカニズムが特定された。

papers.title: BrainAid: Efficient Brain Tumor Detection Using Lightweight CNNs and Explainable AI for Resource-Constrained Environments
papers.summary: A brain tumor is an unusual growth of cells in the brain that can be cancerous or not, affecting normal brain function and causing serious risk to health. Existing solutions for brain tumor classification, such as expert manual evaluations of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, are generally inconsistent as different professionals have different criteria and can be resource-intensive, leading to delayed diagnoses. Additionally, while deep learning models have demonstrated potential, they typically require significant computational resources, motivating the need for more efficient and accessible diagnostic tools that can be deployed in real-time healthcare settings. To address these limitations, this study presents BrainAid, which makes efficient use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for effective classification of four-class classification of glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor MRI scans, outperforming all the standard models such as VGG16, Inception-V3, ResNet-50 and so, while integrating Explainable AI (XAI) to improve interpretability. The BrainAid is trained to classify tumors with a high precision of 98%, achieving an F1 score of 98% and an accuracy of 98% using publicly available dataset. The model is deployed on a Raspberry Pi, demonstrating efficiency in low-resource environments. This system shows the feasibility of real-time, edge-based tumor classification, providing quick diagnostic support for medical professionals and enhancing patient care in resource-limited healthcare facilities and underserved areas.
papers.tldr: BrainAidは、軽量なCNNとExplainable AIを活用して、MRIスキャンから脳腫瘍を高精度（98%）で分類するシステムであり、リソース制約のある環境でも効率的に運用可能です。この技術は、リアルタイムの診断支援を提供し、医療従事者の迅速な判断を助けることを目的としています。

papers.title: Toward a Multimodal Foundation Model for Plasma State Reconstruction
papers.summary: Plasma experiments observe coupled physical states through sparse, heterogeneous, and incomplete diagnostics. We present a proof of concept toward a multimodal foundation model for plasma state reconstruction during magnetic reconnection, motivated by the Facility for Laboratory Reconnection Experiments (FLARE). Using 250 synthetic VPIC simulations at fixed reference electron beta $β_{e0}=0.2$, with 225 training runs and 25 disjoint validation runs, we train a 5.5M-parameter residual 3D U-Net to reconstruct three magnetic-field components and electron density from incomplete observations. The model combines spatial-only pooling, which preserves all 24 temporal frames, with global spatiotemporal self-attention and rotary positional encoding. Independently masking magnetic and density modalities across random, grid, block, and temporal patterns enables sparse sensing, cross-modal completion, density super-resolution, and temporal completion with a single set of weights and no task-specific retraining. With density fully hidden, just 0.1% magnetic spatial visibility reduces median density NRMSE from approximately 0.9 to 0.1. Conversely, observed density improves current-density reconstruction when magnetic data are absent or extremely sparse. With no magnetic observations, roughly 1% density visibility approaches the density reconstruction accuracy achieved with fully observed magnetic fields, although current structure remains more dependent on direct magnetic measurements. Full magnetic conditioning also stabilizes completion of missing future density frames. These results demonstrate bidirectional cross-modal predictive coupling within this simulation regime. Generalization across plasma regimes or to experimental measurements remains untested.
papers.tldr: プラズマ状態再構築のためのマルチモーダル基盤モデルの概念実証を行い、250の合成VPICシミュレーションを用いて、欠損した観測から磁場成分と電子密度を再構築する5.5Mパラメータの3D U-Netを訓練しました。このモデルは、スパースセンシングやクロスモーダル補完を可能にし、観測データの不足に対しても高い再構築精度を示しました。

papers.title: Global Disaster Risk Assessment Using World Risk Index Data: A Geospatial and Visual Analytics Approach
papers.summary: The world has seen several threats that include resource depletion, food security, poverty and inequality, difficulties associated with urbanization, migration, and environmental effects. The World Risk Index (WRI) is a metric that is used to measure the susceptibility of nations against natural disasters and related risks that is reported by the Humanitarian Data Exchange. The WRI is comprised of factors such as susceptibility, vulnerability to natural hazards, and coping mechanisms. The WRI index has allowed to recognize regions in advance in order to face threats and situations beforehand. This study was conducted by analyzing the data that was related to years from 2000 to 2025 using data visualization techniques. Python related libraries of Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Geopandas were used due to their efficiency and usability in analyzing WRI data. As per the analysis, it was identified that countries of Philippines, Mexico, Indonesia, and India were recorded with high WRI index values that showed these nations should be prepared for natural disasters and situations. Hence, this study has provided insights using data visualization techniques in understanding natural disasters and threats so that necessary measures can be taken
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、World Risk Index (WRI) データを用いて、2000年から2025年までの自然災害リスクを地理空間分析とデータ可視化技術で評価し、フィリピン、メキシコ、インドネシア、インドが高いWRI値を示し、自然災害への備えが必要であることを明らかにしました。

papers.title: Exposing AI Inference as a Telco Network API over the 5G User Plane
papers.summary: Supporting edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference as a network service is challenging because current mobile systems can transport tensors but do not expose or understand the inference context that gives those tensors operational meaning. Prior studies have addressed this gap through dynamic partitioning, collaborative inference, and split pipelines; however, these solutions remain application-bound, network-blind, or context-free. This work proposes Inference on Demand (IoD), an inference-on-demand abstraction that exposes split inference through a CAMARA-like Application Program Interface (API) and carries a split-aware tensor context in-band across the 5G user plane path. We evaluate the IoD on a programmable user plane function (UPF)-based testbed using a partitionable visual AI workload, showing that adaptive split selection can operate as a network-facing service while avoiding the rigid cost profile of static configurations. Including our findings, split inference becomes more than offloading when the service intent, runtime partitioning, and tensor transport are made visible to the mobile data plane. This opens a path toward network-native AI services, in which programmable telco infrastructure coordinates computation, context, and connectivity for user-facing applications.
papers.tldr: 5Gユーザープレーンを介してAI推論をネットワークサービスとして提供するための「オンデマンド推論（IoD）」を提案し、動的な分割選択を可能にするAPIを通じて、AI推論の文脈を明示化することで、ネットワークネイティブなAIサービスの実現に向けた道を開くことを示した。

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Semantic Segmentation of Dental Radiographs: Comparative Evaluation of PSPNet, DeepLabv3, UNet, and UNet++
papers.summary: Accurate and efficient analysis of dental radiographs has become increasingly important for disease diagnosis and clinical decision making. In particular, dental radiographs segmentation plays a critical role as it is challenging due to several reasons, such as low contrast, noise in the images, variations in the image quality, etc. Previous studies have primarily addressed these challenges using convolutional neural networks (CNN)-based models. However, direct comparison of these segmentation models is still challenging due to the variations among the experimental settings. Therefore, we mainly compared four segmentation models, including Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSPNet), DeepLabV3, UNet, and UNet++, through a fair, controlled experimentation setting under varying conditions such as image sizes and batch sizes. For this, we used 1269 dental radiography images, and prior to training, we implemented a series of preprocessing techniques. To assess the models, we used several metrics, including Dice coefficient (DICE), Intersection over Union (IoU), accuracy, precision, training and validation losses. According to our results, UNet++ demonstrated the highest IoU score of 0.6719, and a DICE value of 0.7869, showing superior results in terms of segmentation, specifically when configured with an image size of 300x300 and a batch size of 16. In addition, we also explored the effect of image resolutions and batch sizes on model performance and accuracy under different architectures. Therefore, this study provides insights into the strengths of different segmentation models and the potential of deep learning-based semantic segmentation methods for improving automated dental radiograph analysis.
papers.tldr: 深層学習に基づく歯科放射線画像のセマンティックセグメンテーションに関する比較研究では、PSPNet、DeepLabv3、UNet、UNet++の4つのモデルを評価し、UNet++が最高のIoUスコア0.6719とDICE値0.7869を示し、特に300x300の画像サイズとバッチサイズ16で優れた結果を得たことが報告されています。

papers.title: The Optimal Decoder is Tilted Temperature
papers.summary: Larger sample budgets benefit from higher sampling temperatures in LLMs, but what temperature tuning optimizes and why it works remain poorly understood. We seek to answer these questions: we pose decoding as pass@$k$ maximization subject to two constraints that encode critical decoding failure modes: an entropy floor preventing diversity collapse, and a cross-entropy ceiling preventing implausibility. We prove that this maximization takes the form of a single closed-form conditional sampling rule, the \emph{tilted temperature} $q^\star \propto \bigl(p e^{ηV}\bigr)^{1/T}$. Here, the tilt comes from a verifier potential $V$ that quantifies how likely a partial generation is to eventually pass. Ordinary temperature sampling, verifier-greedy decoding, and reward-tilted policies represent special cases. We further show that, under a natural rule for scaling the diversity budget with sample size $k$, the resulting optimal temperature increases with $k$, turning empirical choice into a theorem. The optimum still needs the unknown verifier potential, which we estimate using two design approaches. In the online setting, our J-EOS algorithm jointly tracks the two constraint multipliers and learns the verifier potential from binary pass/ fail feedback alone. In the offline setting, we show that when the model is calibrated, its log-probability tracks correctness up to an affine map. Under this condition, the tilt collapses into the exponent and the optimum reduces to ordinary temperature sampling. Calibrated Temperature Decoding (CTD) then fits one scalar offline and samples with zero additional inference-time overhead relative to temperature sampling. Building on these decision rules, we design a practical decoding algorithm for code generation and evaluate it alongside CTD on benchmarks including HumanEval and MBPP, showing improvements over standard and adaptive decoding baselines.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、LLMにおける最適なデコーダーとして「傾斜温度」を提案し、サンプリング温度の調整がデコーディングの成功率を最大化する方法を明らかにしました。新しいアルゴリズムJ-EOSを用いて、オンラインおよびオフラインの設定で効果的なデコーディングを実現し、標準的なデコーディング手法に対して改善を示しました。

papers.title: Select or Rewrite: Oracle-Guided Fine-Tuning for Generative ASR Post-Editing from N-Best Hypotheses
papers.summary: Large language models can post-edit ASR by using linguistic context to compare N-best hypotheses and rewrite the transcript when needed, often improving WER without retraining the recognizer. However, prompt-only correction is brittle: it may over-edit when top-1 is correct and hallucinate when the reference is absent, and often needs very large models. We propose oracle-guided fine-tuning that turns N-best lists into supervision via three curated pools: corrections (reference in the list but not top-1) to teach selection, regularizers (top-1 correct) to discourage unnecessary rewrites, and hard negatives (reference absent) to suppress hallucination. Fine-tuning on this data provides more effective supervision than random subset fine-tuning for learning a hybrid select-or-rewrite policy, with the clearest gains from around 3B parameters on the proprietary dataset but less conclusive results on CommonVoice, a divergence suggesting that public read-speech text may overlap with LLM pretraining and mask genuine post-editing gains.
papers.tldr: Oracle-guided fine-tuningを用いることで、N-best仮説からのASRのポストエディティングを改善し、選択または書き換えのハイブリッドポリシーを学習する手法を提案。特に、約30億パラメータのモデルで効果的な結果が得られたが、CommonVoiceでは明確な成果が見られなかった。

papers.title: Trace Evolution Bench: Measuring Whether Agents Improve from Their Own Environment Traces
papers.summary: Self-evolving agents are usually scored by endpoint Gain: held-out success after an update minus success before. That difference can credit a frozen rescore as evolution. We introduce Trace Evolution Bench (TEB), a protocol that separates that rescore from a context or weight update, together with three frozen 80/20/40 packs. An update is accepted only when validation does not fall, held-out identifiers never enter the update, and a text update is not ranked with a weight update. The primary scoreboard is coding, graded by hidden unit tests in a closed workspace. On that pack (40 held-out tasks, one family), DeepSeek v4 Pro under no_evolve never changes its policy yet moves 7.5, 5.0, and 12.5 percentage points across three seeds. Of nine text-update cells inspired by GEPA, ACE, and ExpeL, seven have positive excess above that seed's own band, and one gepa_llm seed moves down by the width of its band (-12.5, regression 0.48). GLM and MiniMax do not reproduce that seven-of-nine pattern. No method stays above its own band on every seed of all three models: GLM has two paired cells above their own bands, and MiniMax expel_llm seed 44 is a third (regression 0.30). The methods were fixed on a validation screen before held-out was read. Office, graded by rule-bounded delivery, and manufacturing table QA are separate packs: office DeepSeek does not exceed its own bands (widest 17.5 points), and manufacturing has no paired positive excess beyond its seed band.
papers.tldr: Trace Evolution Bench (TEB)は、自己進化エージェントの評価を改善するためのプロトコルで、更新の際にバリデーションが落ちないことを条件に、エージェントのパフォーマンスを測定します。実験結果では、DeepSeek v4 Proが異なるシードでパフォーマンスを向上させたものの、全てのモデルで一貫した改善は見られませんでした。

papers.title: Use Of Convolutional Neural Networks In Detection Of Branch Dieback Disease In Pequi Trees
papers.summary: This study aims to evaluate and compare convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, specifically AlexNet, Inception, LeNet, VGG16, and MobileNet, for diagnosing branch dieback (seca-dos-ponteiros) in pequi trees (Caryocar brasiliense). This disease represents a severe threat to tree development and fruit yield, causing substantial economic and ecological losses. The methodology implements computer vision techniques using Python libraries, including Scikit-learn, NumPy, TensorFlow, and Matplotlib, to process and evaluate visual data. The CNN models analyze images of leaves, branches, and flower spikes to detect pathological patterns, such as alterations in texture and coloration. Ultimately, this comparative analysis identifies the most effective architecture for accurately distinguishing healthy plants from diseased ones.
papers.tldr: この研究では、Pequiの木における枝の枯死病を診断するために、AlexNet、Inception、LeNet、VGG16、MobileNetといった畳み込みニューラルネットワーク（CNN）アーキテクチャを評価・比較し、視覚データを処理するためにPythonライブラリを使用して、健康な植物と病気の植物を正確に区別する最も効果的なアーキテクチャを特定しています。

papers.title: Belief Embedding Tree Search
papers.summary: Beliefs in a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) are posterior distributions over the hidden state given the agent's history of actions and observations. They summarize everything the history says about the state, so planning in a POMDP is planning in a Markov decision process (MDP) over beliefs. Belief MDPs have continuous state spaces even for finite POMDPs, and exact planning in them is intractable in general. Planners must therefore approximate beliefs and estimate values. Monte Carlo planners do both inside a search tree, with an approximate belief at every node and a value estimate at every leaf. Approximations usually consist of sets of sampled states, with leaf values coming from rollouts, hand-designed bounds, or learned networks. Policies and values computed from these approximations are limited by their quality, and prior methods with learned networks rely on hand-chosen summaries of the sampled states. A belief representation should be computable from the parent node's representation through the POMDP's dynamics, let the search sample from it, and be learned so that it provides the information that policies and value functions need. We present Belief Embedding Tree Search (BETS), a Monte Carlo planner that meets these requirements by representing each node's belief with a generative distribution embedding (GDE) while updating it through the POMDP dynamics. BETS trains its belief model alongside its policy and value networks through experience, with the realized hidden state of the POMDP as the belief model's training target. We evaluate BETS on six configurations of RockSample, LightDark, and PocMan against BetaZero and three planners without learned components. BETS is competitive or leading on all six, while every baseline falls far behind on at least one. Where beliefs are highest-dimensional, it outperforms them by a large margin, even without search.
papers.tldr: Belief Embedding Tree Search (BETS)は、POMDPにおける信念を生成分布埋め込み（GDE）で表現し、POMDPのダイナミクスを通じて更新するモンテカルロプランナーであり、ポリシーや価値ネットワークと共に信念モデルを訓練することで、従来の手法よりも優れた性能を発揮します。実験では、BETSがRockSample、LightDark、PocManの6つの構成で競争力を示し、特に高次元の信念において他の

papers.title: PAT: A Personality-Driven Augmentation and Transfer Learning Framework for Depression Detection on Social Media
papers.summary: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects millions worldwide, with early detection crucial for effective intervention. While exist?ing methods have achieved promising results in automated depression detection, they face two key limitations: (1) noise in post screening: symptom-based semantic screening is easily misled by superficial lexical patterns, thereby introducing false-positive posts; (2) weak op?timization of the post encoder: relying solely on coarse user-level supervision signals pre?vents models from capturing depressive cues within individual posts. To address these limita?tions, we propose PAT, a Personality-driven Augmentation and Transfer learning frame?work. In the first phase, PAT optimizes a post?level encoder via a fine-grained contrastive learning objective, utilizing LLM-based data augmentation driven by classic personality the?ories to alleviate data scarcity. In the second phase, the trained post-level scorer is deployed for high-quality post filtering, while its en?coder parameters are seamlessly transferred for user-level tasks. Extensive experiments demon?strate that PAT significantly outperforms exist?ing methods. Furthermore, PAT delivers multi?granular interpretability by tracing post-level mental-state trajectories and highlighting key symptoms, thereby offering reliable diagnostic evidence for clinical practice.
papers.tldr: PATは、ソーシャルメディア上でのうつ病検出のためのパーソナリティ駆動型の拡張と転移学習フレームワークであり、ポストレベルのエンコーダを最適化し、データ不足を緩和するためにLLMベースのデータ拡張を利用することで、従来の手法を大幅に上回る性能を示します。さらに、PATはポストレベルのメンタルステートの軌跡を追跡し、重要な症状を強調することで、臨床実践における

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Foundations of Online Temperature Sampling
papers.summary: Repetitive, degenerate generation is a persistent failure of LLM decoding, and the standard remedies (temperature, nucleus, and top-$k$ sampling) are static heuristics. By Kac's lemma and the AEP, a stationary source takes time exponential in its entropy to repeat a block. We therefore maximize the entropy of the sampling distributions under one cross-entropy budget that keeps the output plausible under the model. Offline, the solution is temperature sampling, with the inverse temperature as the budget's Lagrange multiplier. \emph{Our contribution is the online problem}: the conditionals $p_1, p_2, \dots$ are revealed one at a time, and the sampling distribution $q_t$ must be chosen causally from $p_1, \dots, p_t$ while the budget couples the entire horizon. The optimal temperature is thus a global shadow price that must be estimated from a prefix. We propose Entropic Online Sampling (EOS), which re-solves for the temperature on each prefix. We prove it loses $O(R\log n)$ entropy against the offline optimum while overshooting the budget by $O(R\log n)$, with $R$ an instance-dependent drift parameter. A budget-tightened variant is exactly feasible at the same rate. Conversely, every exactly feasible online algorithm must lose $Ω(R)$, so EOS is optimal up to a $\log n$ factor. When the conditionals are drawn from a finite mixture, $R=\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$. Experiments confirm that EOS tracks the offline temperature and beats fixed-temperature sampling in entropy.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、オンライン温度サンプリングのためのエントロピックオンラインサンプリング（EOS）を提案し、条件付き確率を逐次的に選択しながら、全体の予算を考慮した最適な温度を推定する手法を示しています。EOSはオフライン最適解に対してエントロピー損失を抑えつつ、固定温度サンプリングよりも優れた結果を示しました。

papers.title: Sparsity Saves Compute, Not Samples: Oracle Inequalities for Dense and Sparse Mixture of Experts
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine specialized experts through an input-dependent routing mechanism, and their sparse variants underpin many modern large-scale systems. Yet the statistical cost of adaptive routing remains only partially understood. We study the estimation error of least-squares MoE estimators when both the experts and the gating network are Lipschitz in their parameters. We represent each MoE as a gate--expert pair in a Gated Hilbert Space, whose norm $\|\cdot\|_Δ$ separates the contributions of routing and expert discrepancies. Using its empirical representation, we derive an oracle inequality with a fast rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal O}\big((Kd_{\mathrm{pr},e}+d_{\mathrm{pr},g})/n\big)$ for dense MoEs with $K$ experts. For sparse Top-$k$ and Top-$p$ routing, the selection map is discontinuous in the gating parameters. We handle this by partitioning the gating class according to the selection patterns it induces on the sample. The resulting bounds match the dense rate up to an additive routing cost governed by the Natarajan dimension of the selector. We show that such a routing-complexity condition cannot be dropped: Lipschitz continuity in the parameters alone does not suffice. For linear softmax gating, the routing cost is of the same order as the gating term. Finally, for linear experts, we establish a matching minimax lower bound of order $Kd_{\mathrm{pr},e}/n$, showing that the rates are optimal up to logarithmic factors.
papers.tldr: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)モデルのスパースバリアントにおける適応ルーティングの統計的コストを研究し、ゲートとエキスパートのパラメータがリプシッツ連続である場合の推定誤差を解析した。結果として、密なMoEとスパースTop-$k$およびTop-$p$ルーティングに対するオラクル不等式を導出し、ルーティングの複雑性条件が重要であることを示した。

papers.title: What Really Works for Universal Multimodal Embeddings? A Controlled Study of Contrastive Training Strategies
papers.summary: Contrastive learning has become the standard paradigm for multimodal representation learning, aligning semantically matched pairs while separating mismatched ones in a shared embedding space. Although various contrastive training strategies have been proposed across negative selection, batch construction, and gradient modulation, their actual effectiveness under controlled, reproducible conditions remains poorly understood. This motivates a fundamental question: Do sophisticated contrastive strategies consistently bring meaningful downstream gains in multimodal embedding learning? To address this, we systematically evaluate representative strategies under a unified benchmarking framework on MMEB. Surprisingly, direct evaluations reveal that most existing strategies offer marginal gains over a standard aligned baseline, with several even degrading overall performance. To uncover the underlying failure modes, we introduce an MLLM-as-a-Judge diagnostic framework that dissects top-1 retrieval behaviors into labeled positives, false negatives (unlabeled valid matches), and hard/easy negative errors. Our systematic analysis yields three key insights: (1) Gradient distortion: Upweighting gradients from high-similarity negatives consistently hurts downstream generalization; (2) Distribution illusion: Wider separation between positive and negative similarity distributions does not necessarily translate to better retrieval performance; and (3) Synergistic training: While false-negative mitigation or hard-batch construction yields limited gains in isolation, integrating hard-negative mining, false-negative mitigation, and hard-batch construction achieves optimal performance, delivering an average improvement of 6.0% on MMEB with Qwen2-VL-2B. Overall, our findings demystify popular contrastive strategies and provide actionable recipes for training universal multimodal embedding models.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、対照的学習戦略の効果を体系的に評価し、ほとんどの既存戦略が標準的なベースラインに対してわずかな改善しかもたらさないことを明らかにしました。また、最適なパフォーマンスを達成するためには、ハードネガティブマイニングや偽陰性の軽減を統合することが重要であると示しています。

papers.title: What Drives AI Citations? Content, Retrieval and Model Knowledge in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
papers.summary: Generative search engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity now decide which Web pages users see as sources, and a growing industry of generative engine optimization advises publishers on how to earn these citations. We study what shapes citation in two 90-day collections of answers to commercial questions in contrasting markets: 158,099 answers with 468,037 citations. Comparing pages of the same website, content matters in one way: pages whose title and paragraphs match the questions people ask are cited more, whereas FAQ blocks, structured data, summary boxes and page speed appear effective only across websites. Page properties nevertheless explain little of the variation between pages of a website. Replaying the questions through the engines' APIs shows why. Every page ChatGPT cites is one its own search retrieved, and which pages that search retrieves, for sub-queries the model rewrites on every answer and that rarely coincide with Google's or Bing's results, explains far more of the variation than page properties (32% against 2.8%). Content acts mainly through this step, by matching the engine's queries in meaning. The model's own knowledge shapes it too: ChatGPT writes brands it knows into its searches, prefers websites it knows, and names brands without any supporting page, and controlled experiments show that brand names reorder its rankings of products with identical facts. Pages are thus cited when searched; brands are also named when remembered. The findings replicate in a market of small B2B vendors. We release data and code.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: ジェネレーティブ検索エンジン（例：ChatGPT）は、ユーザーが見るWebページの引用を決定し、コンテンツの質やページのプロパティよりも、エンジンの検索結果やモデルの知識が引用に大きな影響を与えることが示された。特に、質問に対するページのタイトルや段落が一致することが重要であり、ブランド名も引用順位に影響を及ぼす。

papers.title: InCLAD: A Continual Learning Benchmark for Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Industrial anomaly detection benchmarks have advanced rapidly, yet they remain largely static and therefore underrepresent deployment settings in which inspection systems must be extended from one industrial component to another over time. In our setting, continual industrial anomaly detection is framed as a task-incremental problem: each component defines a task, while the learning objective remains semi-supervised. The goal extends beyond conventional anomaly detection, since models should preserve their performance on all components as they are sequentially exposed to new components. This framing is especially relevant because many existing industrial pipelines either assume fully supervised defect labels or study only isolated datasets, leaving open the question of how semi-supervised anomaly detectors behave across a sequence of heterogeneous components. We address this gap by organizing the benchmark as a sequence of related component-level tasks and by defining multiple scenarios, including random, easy-to-hard, and hard-to-easy. In addition to single-dataset continual scenarios, we propose challenging scenarios spanning across multiple datasets. We further evaluate continual performance from two complementary perspectives: image-level anomaly detection and pixel-level anomaly localization. By recasting industrial anomaly detection as a continual benchmark rather than a static train/test problem, our work establishes a concrete path toward studying knowledge retention, adaptation, and generalization in evolving industrial environments.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: InCLADは、産業用視覚異常検出のための継続的学習ベンチマークであり、異なる産業コンポーネントに対するタスクを逐次的に学習しながら、半教師ありの異常検出性能を維持することを目的としています。これにより、知識の保持や適応、一般化を研究するための具体的な道筋が示されます。

papers.title: Appearance Compensation in Volume Rendering
papers.summary: Can a volume that reproduces every external RGB view still have an incorrect density? We study this question in emission-absorption rendering with an independently parameterized, physically bounded effective source. Appearance compensates a density change by replacing the radiance that it removes from the rest of each ray. We characterize the surviving density information with a shared spatial appearance field. Our first result is an optimal density-only gain after finite-degree spherical-harmonic source refitting. A coupled tensor gauge and physical localized packets identify the sharp limiting nonlinear inverse coefficient as its reciprocal. Our second result realizes positive gain at every fixed finite degree for a residual set of isotropic spatial sources at one fixed density. At the same references, growing angular capacity hides a fixed nonzero density error while retaining physicality and any prescribed finite set of smoothness bounds. Local identifiability and the absence of a capacity-uniform recovery modulus therefore coexist. Our third result constructs an exact physical SH2 ambiguity: central density doubles and relative density $L^2$ error exceeds $14.52\%$, yet every external RGB ray is unchanged. We connect these continuum results to shared finite representations, continuous pixel measurements and density-sensitive acquisition. Complete-class certificates separate SH0, SH1 and SH2 fits at one learned density. Finite-camera results expose the distinct role of spatial capacity, and transmission measurements separate otherwise identical RGB fields. Controlled training tests and captured-smoke profiles supply mechanism evidence with explicit observation scopes. The results show why rendering accuracy alone cannot certify density: recovery also depends on appearance capacity, spatial resolution and measurement design.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、エミッション-吸収レンダリングにおける外部RGBビューを再現しつつも不正確な密度を持つボリュームの可能性を探求し、外観が密度変化を補償するメカニズムを明らかにしました。最適な密度のみの利得や、密度エラーが存在しながらも外部RGBレイが変わらない状況を示し、レンダリング精度だけでは密度を保証できない理由を説明しています。

papers.title: Toward System One Clinical Intelligence: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Counterfactual Explainability of Decision Foundation Models
papers.summary: Automated disease classification from patient-reported symptoms requires balancing the speed of lightweight discriminative models against the contextual understanding and latency costs of autoregressive large language models (LLMs). Decision foundation models offer an alternative by mapping representations directly to candidate classes without free-form text generation. We adapt Clef-Flash, a 9-billion-parameter decision model built on a Qwen3.5 backbone, for 24-class disease classification on the Symptom2Disease benchmark. Using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) with differential learning rates and a stratified split of 960 training and 240 test cases, the model achieves 95.42% diagnostic accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.9551. This improves upon the reported zero-shot baselines of 61.67% for a remote API and 65.00% for a local unadapted initialization, and outperforms the ClinicalBERT baseline (90.90%). By evaluating candidate logits in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding, inference takes under 80 milliseconds per record on a single GPU, yielding a reported 31-fold speedup over generative LLM baselines. To examine symptom-level evidence, we introduce a Leave-One-Symptom-Out (LOSO) counterfactual perturbation framework. Removing disease-defining symptom clauses in a psoriasis example reduces predicted-class confidence from 100.00% to 0.12% and shifts the prediction to impetigo with 99.59% confidence, while removing secondary systemic symptoms produces less than 0.01% change in confidence. These findings suggest that decision-based architectures can combine the linguistic capabilities of large foundation models with low-latency inference and symptom-level interpretability for clinical triage.
papers.tldr: 決定基盤モデルを用いた自動疾病分類に関する研究では、9億パラメータのClef-Flashモデルを適応させ、24クラスの疾病分類で95.42%の診断精度を達成し、従来の生成型LLMに比べて31倍の推論速度向上を実現しました。また、症状レベルの証拠を評価するための新たなフレームワークも導入されています。

papers.title: UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training
papers.summary: Recent bidirectional encoders have been modernized with innovations from causal large language models (LLMs). However, the pretraining recipe itself remains inherited from small-scale conventions, leaving encoders underoptimized, with no single model performing competitively across both classification and retrieval tasks. In this work, we investigate how far encoder performance can be pushed by revisiting core design choices in training, revealing three key findings: (1) Encoders saturate on downstream tasks beyond a few trillion tokens, indicating that additional compute past this point does not help. (2) Across model sizes, lower masking ratios benefit classification while higher ones benefit retrieval, contradicting prior work suggesting larger ratios for larger models. (3) Distillation with pruning improves classification at low masking ratios but degrades retrieval at high ones. Guided by these findings, we present UltraBERT, a single encoder that assigns separate LM heads to low and high masking ratios within a batch and restricts the distillation objective to the low ratio. To our knowledge, UltraBERT is the first encoder to achieve state of the art on both classification and retrieval tasks, reaching 91.0 on GLUE and 47.7 on BEIR. Together, these results show how far encoder performance can be pushed and provide a principled basis for compute allocation, masking ratio design, and knowledge transfer in bidirectional models.
papers.tldr: UltraBERTは、BERTの事前学習の限界を超え、分類と検索タスクの両方で最先端の性能を達成したエンコーダーであり、トークン数やマスキング比率の設計に関する新たな知見を提供しています。

papers.title: PATTERN Can Be Solved from Memory: Generator-Aware Baselines for Synthetic Node Classification
papers.summary: PATTERN, a synthetic node-classification benchmark still used to rank graph networks, plants a random subgraph in a random host graph and asks which nodes belong to it. Its generator draws 100 patterns once and plants the same ones in every split, so each test graph carries a pattern that also appears in 100 training graphs. A matcher that reads these patterns off the training labels and looks them up in each test graph reaches 99.2 class-weighted accuracy with no trained parameters, against 89.8 for the best published model. Inference under the generator without the patterns reaches 86.8. Two published models, CKGConv and GRIT, score lower on patterns they have not seen: on new graphs with fresh patterns both fall below this pattern-blind predictor, and withholding patterns from CKGConv's training lowers its accuracy on the test graphs that carry them. Training CKGConv with a new pattern in every graph raises its accuracy on fresh patterns by about 2 points, to the level of the pattern-blind predictor, at some cost on the reused patterns. The same kind of inference under the generator matches the best published result on CLUSTER and, without any training, scores above every published result we found on Minesweeper's released board. We recommend that synthetic benchmarks report scores on fresh templates beside reused ones, publish baselines built from their generators, and state how their metric is weighted and pooled.
papers.tldr: PATTERNは、合成ノード分類のベンチマークであり、トレーニングデータからパターンを読み取るマッチャーが99.2の精度を達成する一方で、他のモデルは新しいパターンに対して低いスコアを示すことが明らかになった。合成ベンチマークは、新しいテンプレートに基づくスコアを報告し、生成器からのベースラインを公開することが推奨される。

papers.title: Algorithmic Fairness Over Time: Advances & Prospects
papers.summary: In the presence of feedback loops, algorithmic decisions at one time step can influence observed data in subsequent steps, potentially introducing selection bias or shifts in data distribution. Research has demonstrated that ignoring these effects can lead to unfairness, which may worsen over time as the model remains deployed within society. This raises important questions of how to measure and ensure fairness of algorithmic decision-making models over time. In this short paper, we present a taxonomy that distinguishes between different types of static and temporal fairness notions in recent advancements. We then suggest prospects for future research by identifying common implicit temporal assumptions, open questions to enhance our temporal understanding of fairness, and other open challenges.
papers.tldr: アルゴリズムの決定が時間とともにデータに与える影響を無視すると、不公平が生じる可能性があり、これは社会におけるモデルの展開によって悪化することがある。本論文では、静的および時間的な公平性の概念を区別する分類法を提示し、今後の研究の展望を示す。

papers.title: CowCare: A Unified Visual Framework for Viewpoint-Robust Cattle Tracking and Spatiotemporal Heat-Stress Analysis
papers.summary: Reliable individual monitoring is essential for dairy cattle welfare and early heat stress detection in Precision Livestock Farming (PLF). However, translating raw multi-camera videos into automated diagnostics remains challenging due to disconnected tracking and recognition pipelines and complex physical environments. Dense mutual occlusions and cross-camera viewpoint variations fragment identities, while environmental noise, including camera vibrations, and limited agricultural data obscure subtle heat stress cues such as rapid breathing and flank undulations. To bridge low-level visual features and high-level behavioral diagnostics, we propose CowCare, a unified framework combining viewpoint-robust tracking with spatiotemporal heat stress recognition. Its tracking module, CowTrack, maintains cross-camera identity consistency through a View-Decoupled Aggregation Network (VDA-Net). Instead of relying on static global representations, VDA-Net aggregates localized textures under heavy occlusion and uses a Viewpoint Decoupling Transformer (VDT) to suppress transient viewpoint variations. CowTrack further incorporates a causal online self-supervision mechanism for continuous adaptation to dynamic farm scenes. The resulting tracklets are subsequently processed by TSDF-Net, a fine-grained video understanding network. Its Temporal Stabilization and Aggregation Module (TSAM) suppresses high-frequency jitter, while a Diffusion Semantic Prior (DSP) uses frozen pre-trained diffusion semantics to enhance subtle behavioral signals and mitigate overfitting. Extensive evaluations on two real-world farm benchmarks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness: CowTrack achieves 83.48% HOTA and 87.72% IDF1 for global multi-object tracking on MVCow, and TSDF-Net achieves 87.72% Top-1 accuracy on HSCow. These results establish CowCare as a robust end-to-end framework for automated livestock health monitoring.
papers.tldr: CowCareは、視点に強い追跡と時空間的熱ストレス認識を統合したフレームワークで、牛の個体モニタリングと熱ストレスの早期検出を向上させることを目的としています。CowTrackモジュールは、視点の変動を抑えつつ、動的な農場環境に適応するための自己監視機構を取り入れ、実世界の農場ベンチマークで高い精度を達成しました。

papers.title: Conformal Sequential Decision Making With Cost and Sublinear Policy Regret Guarantees
papers.summary: Automated decision makers, such as AI agents that control robots or network devices, must often satisfy hard cost constraints while maintaining competitive performance. In such settings, a cost measure, such as a safety violation rate, energy consumption, or a distortion level, must stay within a given budget in every episode of operation. Furthermore, a cumulative reward metric, accounting for per-step performance, must stay close to the reward of a meaningful reference policy. We formulate this setup as an episodic sequential decision problem in which the state sequence is arbitrary, and the reward and cost may depend on past actions within the same episode. We propose the online conformal episodic agent (OCEA), a policy that selects one candidate action per episode using a regret-controlled algorithm, and switches to a zero-cost action when the remaining budget cannot absorb the maximum cost of one more round. We prove that OCEA satisfies per-episode cost constraints for every state sequence and for every realization of its internal randomness, while achieving a sublinear expected policy regret with respect to the best action sequence in hindsight from a comparator class satisfying the same per-episode cost constraints. We apply OCEA to risk-averse control and online compression with distortion guarantees.
papers.tldr: 自動化された意思決定者は、コスト制約を満たしつつ競争力のあるパフォーマンスを維持する必要があり、提案されたオンライン準拠エピソディックエージェント（OCEA）は、各エピソードで候補アクションを選択し、コストが予算を超える場合にはゼロコストアクションに切り替えることで、コスト制約を満たしつつサブリニアなポリシーの後悔を達成することが証明されています。

papers.title: On the Complexity Gap Between POMDPs and Multi-Environment POMDPs
papers.summary: Multi-environment POMDPs (ME-POMDPs) generalize POMDPs by encoding a finite set of possible environments, capturing model uncertainty. The finite-horizon robust reward maximization problem for a ME-POMDP asks for a policy that maximizes reward in the worst environment, and recent work has shown this problem to be $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete. We expand the complexity landscape of ME-POMDPs by identifying which subclasses retain this $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-completeness. In particular, we take subclasses of POMDPs that are tractable in the single-environment case, and investigate the computational complexity of these classes when extended to the multi-environment setting. We first prove the $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness of multi-environment blind MDPs and deterministic POMDPs using a certain closure-under-mixture condition. We then prove $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-completeness for a range of subclasses that do not satisfy that closure condition, yielding new complexity results for multi-observation POMDPs. Finally, we show existential theory of the reals ($\exists \mathbb{R}$)-completeness for numerous ME-POMDP problems under time-dependent Markovian policies or finite-state controllers that are $\mathsf{NP}$-complete for standard POMDPs. These results reveal a subtle relationship between POMDP and ME-POMDP complexity that depends heavily on the subclasses involved.
papers.tldr: ME-POMDPsはPOMDPsを一般化し、モデル不確実性を捉えるが、最悪環境での報酬最大化問題は$\mathsf{PSPACE}$-完全であることが示された。特定のサブクラスがこの複雑性を保持するかどうかを調査し、いくつかの新しい複雑性結果を明らかにした。

papers.title: Can You Trust Your Preference Models? Stackelberg Games for Alignment
papers.summary: Language models are frequently aligned to human preferences via imperfect evaluators whose errors can be exploited during optimization. We train policies to search for comparisons on which an evaluator may reverse the underlying preference, providing candidates for additional supervision. Since human preferences are unavailable during policy training, we use disagreement among an ensemble of preference models as a proxy for prediction error. We formulate this search as a zero-sum Stackelberg game between two opposing policies, a Leader which tries to minimize disagreement, and a Follower which maximizes it. For a general class of finite contextual Stackelberg games, we establish equilibrium existence and, under regularization, uniqueness and a closed-form characterization. We introduce Stackelberg Mirror Descent-Ascent (SMIDA), a two-timescale algorithm with linear last-iterate convergence in the tabular setting, and develop a neural policy-gradient analogue. Experiments with a synthetic oracle support disagreement as an informative proxy for prediction error. On held out data the trained policies outperform reference policies and increase the fraction of comparisons that exceed a disagreement threshold and reverse the oracle's preference.
papers.tldr: 言語モデルの人間の好みに対する整合性を向上させるため、Stackelbergゲームを用いて評価者の誤りを利用し、ポリシーを訓練する手法を提案します。実験では、訓練されたポリシーが参照ポリシーを上回り、評価者の好みを逆転させる比較の割合を増加させることが示されました。

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.summary: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: DisCo代数は、確率の結合と分解を扱う新しい枠組みで、結合の後に分解を行うと元の情報を再構築できるが、逆は成り立たず、情報損失は条件付きKLダイバージェンスによって示される。この非対称性は、スカラーのブロック要約が捉えられる交差ブロック依存の限界を明らかにする。

papers.title: Retraining-Free Depth Pruning of Vision Transformers: A Cross Domain Study of Layer Redundancy
papers.summary: Transformer architectures have achieved strong results in natural language processing and computer vision, but their deployment is limited by high computational, memory and storage costs, motivating research into model compression techniques, such as pruning, while preserving performance. Prior work has shown substantial redundancy in large language models (LLMs), and redundancy in vision transformers has also been investigated, but it remains less systematically analyzed than in LLMs. In this work, we extend similarity-based redundancy analysis to vision models by measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify transformations with minimal impact. We study redundancy patterns across several transformer architectures and find that deep vision transformers such as DINOv2 and SwinV2, like language models, exhibit significant redundancy. We then evaluate how this redundancy can be exploited to improve efficiency, analyzing the trade-off between inference speed and performance degradation under different pruning strategies. Our results show that moderate pruning can yield substantial acceleration with limited impact on accuracy, and that 20% of the DINOv2 blocks can be removed without any retraining, for a 1.24x throughput gain and a 20% lower energy per image at a relative accuracy loss below 1% on ImageNet-1K. We further propose a model selection pipeline that automatically identifies the best pruned configuration for a given dataset, reducing FLOPs by 13% to 27% on average across architectures with an average accuracy change between -0.3 and +1.0 points.
papers.tldr: 深層ビジョントランスフォーマーにおける冗長性を分析し、プルーニングを通じて効率を向上させる手法を提案。特に、DINOv2の20%のブロックを再学習なしで削除することで、1.24倍のスループット向上と20%のエネルギー削減を実現し、精度の低下は1%未満に抑えられることを示した。

papers.title: DiffGA: Steering Frozen Diffusion Models for Materials Design via Evolutionary Search
papers.summary: Steering candidate generation toward user-defined objectives is central to inverse materials design, yet remains difficult when objectives are black-box, changing, or non-differentiable, as in many simulation- and experiment-derived properties. Generative models offer a solution but typically require retraining or fine-tuning for each new objective, demanding labeled data and substantial compute, or rely on differentiable guidance that is brittle to gradient noise and undefined for many practical targets. We present DiffGA, a retraining-free framework that injects evolutionary search into the sampling trajectory of a retrained diffusion model, evolving partially denoised states under an arbitrary black-box oracle. Because oracle evaluation often dominates campaign cost, we couple DiffGA with an on-the-fly Bayesian surrogate that reuses representations from state-of-the-art machine-learned force fields (MLFFs). A Gaussian process is fit during the campaign on the force fields's graph embeddings and, once it demonstrably ranks an unseen generation, replaces expensive property evaluations under an uncertainty-aware acquisition rule, reducing oracle cost with negligible loss of accuracy. Across three crystal-design tasks using a frozen MatterGen backbone, DiffGA outperforms diffusion-only, compute-matched, purely evolutionary, and fine-tuned baselines in oracle-assessed rates of stable, unique, and novel hits. Rather than proposing scientific compounds, we use density functional theory to quantify MLFF oracle fidelity, showing that it is a faithful proxy in key regimes but systematically biased in others, delineating when proxy-driven generative discovery can be trusted. On a representative sample, DiffGA's top hits survive first principles re-evaluation as physically realistic hits, while the surrogate-accelerated pipeline preserves this fidelity at a fraction of the cost.
papers.tldr: DiffGAは、ユーザー定義の目的に向けて進化的探索を取り入れたフレームワークで、再訓練なしで凍結された拡散モデルを利用し、黒箱オラクルの下で部分的にデノイズされた状態を進化させることで、材料設計を効率化します。この手法は、ベイズサロゲートを組み合わせることで、コストを削減しつつ高い精度を維持し、さまざまな結晶設計タスクで従来の手法を上回る成果を示しています。

papers.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.summary: Tabular foundation models adapt to new datasets through in-context learning (ICL), and, like most transformers, they tie computational depth to the number of independently parameterized layers. We ask whether the ICL stage of such a model needs a distinct set of parameters for every layer, or only depth. We introduce Tab-Loop, which replaces the 12 untied ICL blocks of TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied $k$ times and changes nothing else: the encoders, decoder, synthetic prior and training recipe are shared with an untied baseline trained for the same compute. At matched pretraining compute (18.2 EFLOP) and matched inference compute (12 block applications), Tab-Loop matches the baseline with 62\% fewer parameters (10.4M vs.\ 27.6M): held-out log loss is 0.4583 vs.\ 0.4588, mean accuracy on 200 TALENT datasets is 84.10\% vs.\ 83.92\%, and Elo on 38 TabArena datasets is 1409 vs.\ 1396. A 4-block untied control with Tab-Loop's parameter count, which sees 32\% more training tables for the same compute, trails both (83.46\%; Elo 1343). Because weights are shared, depth becomes a choice made at inference. Accuracy rises with the number of loops through the trained range and holds beyond it, and continued training with deeper loops extends the useful range, reaching the baseline's stage-2 scores at 4--5$\times$ its inference compute. At this scale, the ICL stage of a tabular foundation model needs depth more than it needs distinct parameters.
papers.tldr: Tab-Loopは、タブラー基盤モデルのインコンテキスト学習（ICL）において、12の独立したブロックを4つの結合ブロックに置き換えることで、62%少ないパラメータで同等の性能を達成する手法を提案しており、深さが重要であることを示しています。

papers.title: Certify the Decision, Not Every Score: Exact Top-k Selection from Few Evaluations
papers.summary: Choosing a few robust algorithms or schedules can require evaluating every candidate under many adverse scenarios, even though an agent only needs to identify the winners. A predictor may suggest those winners, but cannot rule out a surprise in an unevaluated scenario. We introduce Certified Adaptive Selection (CAS), which returns the exact top-$k$ set as soon as remaining uncertainty cannot change it. CAS keeps guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Expected Shortfall (ES), the average loss in the worst scenarios. Its stopping test compares the worst admissible selected candidate with the best admissible excluded one; for information-disjoint Cartesian intervals this one-cut test is necessary and sufficient. Prediction has a separate role: selecting the next outcome to evaluate, never authorizing the decision. For empirical ES with exact unit-cost queries, we compute in polynomial time the fewest evaluations that could have proved the realized decision in hindsight. Our prediction-guided agent CAS-PG is exact for every predictor, including adversarial ones. On two public algorithm-selection matrices, CAS-PG certifies the exact top three after 630 of 3150 and 981 of 2200 replayed queries, or $1.14$ and $1.18$ times that hindsight minimum. Without historical outcomes, its transcript-only variant requires $1.28$ and $1.37$ times the minimum, outperforming the tested non-predictive certified policies. Separately, a prediction-free CAS policy avoids $93.0\%$ of exact recourse solves in synthetic energy scheduling. One certificate thus supports several acquisition policies and separately proved risk/cost extensions: prediction changes the work, not the justified choice.
papers.tldr: Certified Adaptive Selection (CAS)は、残りの不確実性が結果を変えられないと判断した時点で、正確なトップ-kの選択を行う手法であり、予測は次の評価対象を選ぶ役割を果たすが、決定を承認することはない。CAS-PGは、予測に基づいて少ない評価で正確な結果を証明し、従来のポリシーよりも優れた性能を示す。

papers.title: Characterizing the Separability Gap in Prior-Data Fitted Networks
